title: Copy and paste chords in the terminal on Linux
why: Upstream, the terminal has no copy or paste chord on Linux. The custom key handler of the plugin (class Gc) handles only Shift+Enter there, so each clipboard chord depends on the default action of Chromium in the hidden helper textarea of xterm.js. Ctrl+Shift+C does nothing: xterm.js makes no key for it, and Chromium has no edit command for it. Ctrl+Insert (the chord that the Omarchy universal clipboard sends for Super+C to a window with the tag terminal) runs the Chromium Copy command on the DOM selection of the textarea, not on the xterm.js selection. xterm.js fills that textarea only after a mouse selection on Linux, so the copy fails or copies old text. Chromium also matches the modifiers of an edit command exactly, so a Super modifier in the sent event stops the Insert chords. The edit adds a key handler before the upstream handler. On every platform except macOS (A2.CURRENT is not "darwin"), Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+Insert copy the xterm.js selection with navigator.clipboard.writeText, and Ctrl+Shift+V and Shift+Insert paste with navigator.clipboard.readText and paste() of xterm.js (the clipboard API of the right-click action of the plugin; paste() keeps the bracketed paste mode). On keydown it stops the default action, so a paste never occurs two times. The handler reads only keydown and keyup: a keypress carries a character code in keyCode (45 is "-"). A copy chord with no selection does nothing. The selection stays after a copy. The Insert chords ignore the Super modifier. The C and V chords need exactly Ctrl+Shift. Alt cancels every chord. Ctrl+C keeps sending ^C (SIGINT), also with a selection: that is the Linux terminal standard, and Ctrl+C is the interrupt key of a running agent. Ctrl+V keeps sending ^V. macOS does not change.
